title: Sea Surface Temperature
what_it_is: How warm the top few meters of ocean water are, in °C. Measured by buoys and satellites.
why_it_matters: Small rises (even 0.5–1°C) can drive coral bleaching, shift fish habitats, and hurt spawning.

title: Salinity
what_it_is: How much salt is dissolved in the water, in practical salinity units (psu).
why_it_matters: Freshwater runoff and evaporation change salinity, which affects which species can live where.

title: Chlorophyll-a
what_it_is: A proxy for how much microscopic plant life (phytoplankton) is in the water, in mg/m³.
why_it_matters: Phytoplankton is the base of the marine food chain — a drop here often shows up as a fish-catch decline months later.

title: Degree Heating Weeks (DHW)
what_it_is: A running total of how far above normal, and for how long, sea temperature has been at a reef site.
why_it_matters: It's the standard early-warning number for coral bleaching risk — the higher it climbs, the more likely bleaching becomes.

title: eDNA Confidence
what_it_is: How sure the lab's classification pipeline is that a genetic fragment found in a water sample belongs to a given species.
why_it_matters: eDNA can detect species without ever seeing or catching them — useful for rare or shy species — but confidence tells you how much to trust a given match.

title: Conservation Status
what_it_is: IUCN Red List category — Least Concern, Near Threatened, Vulnerable, Endangered.
why_it_matters: It's the standard, internationally recognized measure of a species' extinction risk.

title: Fishing / Conservation Advisory
what_it_is: An active recommendation to reduce fishing pressure or protect habitat in a specific region, issued when catch or sensor data crosses a concerning threshold.
why_it_matters: Advisories are the actionable output of all this monitoring — the point where data turns into a recommendation someone can act on.

title: Vessel Tracking
what_it_is: Ship positions broadcast via AIS (Automatic Identification System) and cross-checked against protected-area boundaries.
why_it_matters: It's how illegal fishing inside marine protected areas gets caught — a boat with no business being there, sitting still or trawling.

title: Marine Protected Area (MPA)
what_it_is: A defined ocean zone where fishing, dredging, or other extractive activity is restricted or banned by law.
why_it_matters: MPAs only work if violations are actually detected — most rely on patrol boats or self-reporting, which is why vessel tracking matters.

title: Treatment Plant Compliance
what_it_is: Whether a coastal sewage/effluent treatment plant meets discharge standards set by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
why_it_matters: Non-compliant discharge is a direct, local driver of coastal water quality decline — often the real cause behind a biodiversity drop that looks climate-related at first glance.

title: Stock Forecast
what_it_is: A simple trend line fit to recent catch tonnage, projected 6 months ahead with a confidence band.
why_it_matters: It flags direction and rough magnitude early — not a substitute for a full scientific stock assessment, but enough to justify a closer look.

title: Range Shift
what_it_is: A trend line of where a species has actually been observed (latitude) over time, from real occurrence records.
why_it_matters: Species moving toward the poles over years is one of the clearest fingerprints of ocean warming on marine life.

title: Biodiversity Index
what_it_is: A simple count of distinct species observed or detected (survey + eDNA) in a region.
why_it_matters: A rough, comparable stand-in for ecosystem health across regions that otherwise have very different monitoring histories.

title: Composite Bleaching Score
what_it_is: A single 0-100 score combining heat stress buildup (60%), chlorophyll drift (25%), and historical bleaching frequency (15%) — weights are fixed and shown alongside the score, not hidden.
why_it_matters: One number is easier to act on than three separate charts, but only if you can see what it's made of — the factor breakdown is what keeps it from being a black box.

title: Species Movement Trajectory
what_it_is: The year-by-year center point of where a species has been recorded, smoothed to reduce noise, with a short forecast continuation based on its recent direction of travel.
why_it_matters: A moving centroid over real years of records is a more honest picture of range shift than a single trend line — you can see the actual path, not just its slope.

title: What-If Scenario Simulator
what_it_is: Sliders for SST anomaly, fishing pressure, and chlorophyll delta that re-run the real stock/bleaching/range-shift models with a hypothetical input instead of the recorded one.
why_it_matters: Turns a static chart into something you can operate — see how a warmer season or heavier fishing would change the outlook, clearly separate from the live forecast.
